technical-knowledge.question: Do I need any technical knowledge to work with you?
technical-knowledge.answer: Not at all. I handle the entire lifecycle—from domain configuration and hosting setup to deployment. Once live, I will provide a simple walk-through so you can manage your operations or text updates effortlessly.

code-ownership.question: Who owns the source code and project assets after delivery?
code-ownership.answer: You do. You retain 100% intellectual property and ownership. Upon project completion, the entire repository and production assets are securely handed over to your GitHub or cloud account.

retainer-model.question: How does the 'Fixed Developer Retainer' model work?
retainer-model.answer: It is like having a dedicated Remote CTO/Engineer on demand without the full-time overhead. For a fixed monthly fee, I take care of your priority updates, continuous performance tuning, server security audits, and urgent bug fixes — keeping your systems updated, monitored, and quickly repaired.

communication-timezone.question: How do we handle communication and timezone differences?
communication-timezone.answer: I am based in Bangladesh but maintain highly flexible working hours that overlap perfectly with Australian (AEST) and European/German (CET) business days. We will use tools like Slack, Zoom, and Notion for transparent, structured async and sync updates.

project-timeline.question: What is the typical timeline for a project?
project-timeline.answer: An elite Next.js Website or Conversion Landing Page is typically engineered and deployed within 3 to 7 business days. Complex custom business software or internal infrastructure timelines are calculated based on your specific operational requirements.

hero.title: The engineer behind the work
hero.lead: Who I am, how I got here, and the principles I bring to every system I build.

paragraphs: I'm Md Sahaduzzaman — most people call me Sahad. I'm a software engineer who builds the operational systems businesses quietly depend on: scheduling engines, booking platforms, internal dashboards, APIs, and the databases underneath them.

Since 2024 I've worked professionally with clients and teams in Australia, Germany, South Korea, and Bangladesh — as an employee and, since 2026, as the founder of Sahad Labs. The work ranges from a disability-services platform handling sensitive records to a real-estate booking engine that replaced spreadsheets.
I work end to end: understanding the operation, designing the data model, building the application, and seeing it into production. This page is the longer version of that story.

education.text: Algorithms, databases, networking, web systems, and software engineering — applied in full-stack projects along the way.

taqwa.title: Software Engineer, Taqwa Group
taqwa.text: Sole software engineer for a multi-industry platform: land-plot booking with an installment (EMI) engine, payment-gateway integration, referral and commission logic, and admin dashboards — replacing spreadsheet-driven operations.

rushkat.text: Performance work on a high-traffic store backend: query optimization, Redis caching, and REST APIs for heavy 3D-asset endpoints.

fourj.title: Software Engineer, 4j Traders
fourj.text: Order-processing backend with strict transaction isolation, multi-role RBAC, and the Docker + GitHub Actions pipeline the team now deploys through.

sahadlabs.title: Founder & engineer, Sahad Labs
sahadlabs.text: Delivering client systems end to end — most notably the Cozee Care disability-services platform and the Violina Pflegedienst care platform — alongside my own telemedicine product.

principles.title: How I approach engineering
principles.subtitle: Principles I actually work by — each one earned on a real project.

understand.title: Understand the operation before the architecture
understand.text: The system has to match how the business actually runs, not how a textbook says it should. At Taqwa Group, the installment engine had to compute variable interest across custom repayment tenures — their real rules — before anything else could work.

secure.title: Secure by default, not by afterthought
secure.text: Sensitive data decides the architecture early. For Cozee Care, health-records confidentiality meant route-level authorization with NestJS Guards and JWT — permission boundaries enforced at every endpoint, not sprinkled through page code.

performance.title: Performance is a design decision
performance.text: Speed comes from the data model and query shape, not from late-stage tweaking. At Rushkat and 4j Traders, caching strategy and query optimization were the difference between endpoints that survive concurrent load and ones that don't.

ownership.title: Own it from commit to production
ownership.text: The job ends when it runs in production, safely and repeatably. At 4j Traders I built the Docker and GitHub Actions pipeline the team deploys through; for client systems I handle deployment and handover in the client's own accounts.

handover.title: Leave clients independent
handover.text: You own what I build: source code, repositories, and accounts, handed over at completion, with a plain-language walk-through so your team can run it without me. Dependency is not a business model.

working.title: Working with me
working.subtitle: The parts of the job that aren't code — described the way clients and colleagues have actually experienced it.

timezones.title: Time zones are my problem, not yours
timezones.text: I'm based in Bangladesh and keep working hours that overlap with Australian, European, and US business days. My delivered client work to date sits with teams in Australia and Europe — and my hours are built to cover the US East Coast too.

communication.title: Structured, async-friendly updates
communication.text: Progress lives in writing — Slack, email, Notion — with calls for the decisions that need a voice. You always know what shipped and what's next without chasing me.

plainLanguage.title: No-jargon by default
plainLanguage.text: I explain systems in the language of the operation. Non-technical clients get a simple walk-through at handover so they can run their own system confidently.

confidentiality.title: Discretion with sensitive work
confidentiality.text: Much of my work sits inside regulated or commercially sensitive operations — disability services, healthcare, sales data. I treat what I learn on the job as confidential, and this portfolio only shows what's already public.
